_about: The SOURCE's own notes (the author's/editor's), kept a separate stream from the translator's notes.json. The original gathers nine of them at its end, keyed to bracketed markers [1]..[9] that appear inline in the chapters; each entry here carries that ORIGINAL number in 'n', an 'anchor' (a verbatim substring of the English prose, where the marker is re-attached), and the source note rendered into English. The builder places a bracketed marker in a distinct colour at the anchor and lists these under 'Notes in the Original Edition', so a reader can always tell the author's apparatus from the translator's. Bodies are XHTML: numeric character references, never named entities.

ch01.note: In English in the original; that is, “Light, Heat, Power!”

ch02.note: In those days those who dealt in government bonds were fond of the three issues — Customs (关税), Troop-Disbandment (裁兵), and Reorganization (编遣); but because the market swung so violently, a man dealing in these three bonds would often be worth a vast fortune one day and left bare-handed the next, so wags dubbed such bond-dealers men “at the coffin-edge,” meaning how perilous it was. “Coffin-edge” (棉材边, guancai bian) is in fact a pun on the first characters of “Customs, Troop-Disbandment, Reorganization” (关裁编, guan cai bian).

ch06.note: “Feiyangsan” (绶洋伞) is the transliteration of an English word, meaning “fiancée.”
In English in the original; that is, “poetic and love” (诗意与恋爱, poetry and love).
“Maixie Zeng” (麦歪曾) is French: Monsieur Zeng, that is, “Mr. Zeng.” Du Xintuo studied in France, and so has the habit.
